text: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-04 -- now a MIGRATION-REMEDIATION TRACKER, not a port plan. The original 'port agent-intercom (Rust) to a feature-complete, CGO-free Go implementation' framing is RETIRED, and the Rust repository at C:\Source\GitHub\intercom (softwaresalt/agent-intercom @ 41df772) is DEMOTED from behavioral oracle to HISTORICAL REFERENCE ONLY (governing decision D8). It is NOT an oracle for operator UI, transport, configuration schema, or credentials, and parity with it is NO LONGER a definition of done -- the two products no longer share an operator surface, a transport, or an agent boundary. VOID: the entire P4-P15 successor ordering recorded in this entry (internal/models + SQLite 7-table schema, the remaining repos + retention, the ACP subprocess risk slice with spawner/handshake/codec/reader/writer, AgentDriver + ACP driver, the Slack Socket Mode slice, the Slack surface with slash commands/modals/9 handlers/US17 thread replies, diff-apply/approval/terminal-gate/policy/audit as scoped there, internal/agenttools with the 9 MCP wire tool names, the resilience slice as scoped, IPC + intercom-ctl, the 56/22/46/6 parity corpus sweep, and the cutover-with-Rust-fallback decision). Slack, ACP, and the parity corpus are all retired; the MCP HTTP tool endpoint retention decision (D1) is likewise void because it existed to serve ACP subprocesses. STILL VALID and carried forward: the shipped foundation 001-F/001-S, error taxonomy + path containment 002-F/002-S, and config package 003-F/003-S (the last now under corrective remediation). WHAT THIS ENTRY NOW TRACKS: residual migration cleanup where retired-architecture surfaces survive in shipped code -- currently the internal/apperr Kind taxonomy contamination (stash 8C2D578D) and any further contamination the U-E1a retired-architecture gate surfaces. The forward roadmap is NOT here: it is phases C1-C11 in docs/plans/2026-09-04-intercom-go-architecture-correction-plan.md, governed by docs/decisions/2026-09-04-intercom-go-architecture-correction-copilot-sdk-deliberation.md. The ORACLE CORRECTION recorded in the original text (references\herdr is ogulcancelik/herdr, a Rust terminal multiplexer, NOT an oracle) remains accurate and is preserved; herdr stays untouched, git-excluded, and non-governing. Priority dropped from high to medium: this is cleanup tracking, not a delivery driver.

GOVERNING PRODUCT DIRECTION (corrected 2026-09-04; UNBLOCKED). intercom-go is a per-workspace Go backend brokering a GitHub Copilot agent session between two co-equal operator surfaces: a local Bubble Tea TUI and a remote SPA reached over a Microsoft Dev Tunnel. CORRECTIONS APPLIED to this entry's original text: (1) the remote client is an SPA, NOT iOS -- the iOS wording is stale; SPA framework choice is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE; (2) the agent boundary is the OFFICIAL GitHub Copilot SDK for Go (github.com/github/copilot-sdk/go, pinned v1.0.11 = commit a550258d5c37bd662197536992a23d633bfe5804), NOT coder/acp-go-sdk -- intercom-go implements no ACP broker, no ACP wire protocol, and no direct headless-Copilot-CLI lifecycle. That the SDK internally manages a Copilot CLI server over JSON-RPC is an SDK IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL (its codec is under internal/ and unimportable by hosts); (3) the three load-bearing conflicts recorded here are RESOLVED: durability -- the backend projection is a CACHE and the SDK runtime is the durable event source via GetEvents/ResumeSession, bridged by the D4a minimal session pointer (a pointer, not a store; D7 full persistence remains deferred); operator surface in the persistence schema -- moot, Slack is retired so slack_ts/thread_ts/channel_id vanish with it; lifecycle ownership -- settled as one isolated process per workspace, orchestrated by autoharness, one allocated HTTP/WS port (the second ACP port is gone). (4) The AgentDriver-vs-OperatorGateway distinction recorded here is PRESERVED and now realised: the SDK adapter is the agent-facing side, and the OperatorGateway (event envelopes, hydration/reconnect, first-responder arbitration, WebSocket backpressure) is the operator-facing side. GOVERNING ARTIFACTS: docs/decisions/2026-09-04-intercom-go-architecture-correction-copilot-sdk-deliberation.md; docs/design-docs/intercom-go-backend-architecture.md (revision 2); roadmap and next slice in docs/plans/2026-09-04-intercom-go-architecture-correction-plan.md (phases C1-C11). NEXT SLICE: C1 corrective (config remediation + Go 1.24 floor + anti-regression gate), harvested and queued as a shipment. Open operator decisions carried forward: Q1/H2 Copilot CLI version floor (blocks C2); Q3/H3 Dev Tunnel auth (blocks C10); Q6/H4 sessions-per-process (blocks C9); H5 permission authorization model (blocks C5); H6 session-pointer store semantics (blocks C4). NO BLOCKERS REMAIN for C1.

Add a machine-checkable oracle-drift gate: a script (plus CI wiring) that reads the pinned oracle commit from docs/oracle-pin.md, runs 'git -C <oracle-path> rev-parse HEAD', and fails when it does not match 41df772. Deferred from the 002-S plan review as residual P2 finding ARCH-5: the oracle is out-of-tree so the pin is currently DOCUMENTARY ONLY, which is the weakest link for future dark-factory (unattended) execution of phases P2-P14 - a drifted oracle would silently freeze contracts against the wrong revision with no detection. Kept out of shipment 002-S to avoid expanding a leaf slice with a new script and CI surface. Depends on 002.003.001-ST (docs/oracle-pin.md must exist first). Alternative worth evaluating: vendor the oracle's test fixtures into this repo so parity tests are self-contained and oracle-independent at runtime. Source: docs/plans/2026-09-03-intercom-go-apperr-pathsafe-plan.md, Plan Review residual findings.

internal/apperr error-taxonomy contamination: Kind sentinels KindSlack, KindIPC and KindACP (String() values 'slack', 'ipc', 'acp') are retired-architecture surfaces that survive the 2026-09-04 architecture correction. Found during adversarial plan review of corrective slice C1: the retired-architecture CI gate (U-E1a) originally scoped to internal/** could never pass because of them, so gate scope was narrowed to internal/config/** + config.toml.example + cmd/** and this contamination was deferred rather than absorbed (governing decision D6a). Removing/renaming these Kinds is a separate error-taxonomy CONTRACT change: apperr.Kind is pinned by a sentinel-count/drift test and consumed across the codebase, so it needs its own slice and review. Requires deliberation: yes -- remove outright, rename to architecture-neutral names, or replace with SDK/transport/operator-surface Kinds aligned to the corrected architecture. Interacts with existing stash 7774C9CA (apperr.Kind has no Stringer; kindSentinel has no bounds validation/drift test) -- same taxonomy, should be deliberated together, but they are DISTINCT findings and neither supersedes the other.
